bats and moths have evolved to chase and flee in a way that is mutually beneficial to both species.
bats and moths are engaged in a co-evolutionary arms race that is driven by the evolution of predator and prey flight kinematics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometry of bat–inset interactions is complex and cannot be captured by simple mathematical models.

prey escape success is not determined solely by predator kinematics, but rather by the interaction of the predator’s attack trajectory and the prey’s escape trajectory, and that the prey’s escape angle is a key factor in determining whether it will survive a chase.
prey can use a variety of strategies, not just speed and turning ability, to escape predators.
